quizzes.title: SDR 2026 Findings and India's Position
quizzes.passage:
The Sustainable Development Report is an annual assessment of how countries are progressing towards the Sustainable Development Goals. It gives each country a score on a scale of 0 to 100, which allows countries to be compared with one another. The report covers all UN Member States, and it is linked to the 2030 Agenda, the framework under which the goals were adopted. The goals cover a wide range of areas, including poverty, health, education and climate action.

The latest findings suggest that progress is uneven. A large share of targets is moving forward only slowly, while a smaller group of targets has slipped backwards compared with the position recorded in 2015. Some regions have improved more quickly than others, and the report draws attention to structural problems that affect particular goals.

India is one of the countries covered by the assessment. The report notes that its position has improved over time and that its overall performance has moved upward compared with earlier editions. Even so, only part of India's targets is expected to be achieved by 2030. Many of its targets are advancing at a pace that is insufficient to meet the deadline, and the report describes India's performance in terms of the goals where its progress is weakest.

questions.q: Which body released the 11th Sustainable Development Report 2026?
questions.explanation: The booklet names the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network as the body that released the 2026 report.

questions.q: What is India's overall SDG Index score in the 2026 report?
questions.explanation: India's overall SDG Index score in the 2026 report is 68.3 out of 100.

questions.q: What percentage of India's SDG targets is expected to be achieved by 2030?
questions.explanation: About 33.3% of India's SDG targets are expected to be achieved by 2030.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The report identifies Zero Hunger as India's most critical development challenge.
Reason (R): Around 15% of targets have experienced setbacks compared to their 2015 baseline.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the setback figure does not explain why Zero Hunger is India's critical challenge.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Overall SDG Index score of India   ->   A. 15%
II. India's targets expected to be achieved by 2030   ->   C. 16.5%
III. Global targets with setbacks against the 2015 baseline   ->   D. 33.3%
IV. Global targets progressing as planned   ->   B. 68.3
questions.explanation: The matches are 68.3 for the overall score, 33.3% for 2030 targets, 15% for setbacks and 16.5% for targets progressing as planned.

questions.q:
Read the statements below:
I. The report has been published annually since 2016.
II. Countries are scored on a scale of 0 to 10.
III. Nearly 24% of assessed indicators have deteriorated since the SDGs were adopted.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the scoring scale runs from 0 to 100, not 0 to 10.

questions.q:
Examine the following:
I. The 2026 report is the eleventh edition in the series.
II. The report was released by the United Nations Development Programme.
III. Barbados was the lowest-ranked country on supporting UN-centred multilateral cooperation.
Which option gives the number of correct statements?
questions.explanation: Only statement I is correct, since the UN SDSN released the report and Barbados was the highest-ranked country on that parameter.

quizzes.title: SDG Progress and India in 2026
quizzes.passage:
Progress towards the Sustainable Development Goals is tracked through an annual report, which has been published every year since 2016. The report scores each country on how close it is to achieving the goals, and it covers all UN Member States. Each goal is supported by specific targets, and a country's progress is judged by looking at those targets. The goals were adopted as part of the 2030 Agenda, which set a common deadline for the world to achieve them.

The latest edition finds that many goals are not on course for that deadline. A substantial share of targets is moving forward too slowly to be met in time, while a smaller group has slipped back compared with its starting point. Some regions have recorded rapid gains since 2015, and these gains stand out in the global picture.

India is among the countries assessed. Its position has improved over the years, and the report shows that the country has moved upward in the ranking. However, only part of its targets is expected to be reached on schedule. The report also examines the individual areas where the country's progress is weakest, and it identifies one goal as the most serious challenge for its development.

questions.q: What is India's overall SDG Index score in the 2026 report? (out of 100)
questions.explanation: India's overall SDG Index score is 68.3 out of 100.

questions.q: What percentage of India's SDG targets is expected to be achieved by 2030? (percent)
questions.explanation: About 33.3% of India's SDG targets are expected to be achieved by 2030.

questions.q: Which network released the 11th Sustainable Development Report 2026? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The report was released by the UN Sustainable Development Solutions Network, abbreviated UN SDSN.

questions.q: Which two regions are described as the fastest-improving regions in SDG progress since 2015? (name both)
questions.explanation: The report says East and South Asia lead global SDG progress and are the fastest-improving regions since 2015.

questions.q: Approximately what percentage of global SDG targets are progressing as planned? (percent)
questions.explanation: Approximately 16.5% of SDG targets are progressing as planned.

questions.q: Nearly what percentage of assessed indicators have deteriorated since the SDGs were adopted? (percent)
questions.explanation: Nearly 24% of assessed indicators have deteriorated since the SDGs were adopted.

questions.q: Which SDG is identified as India's most critical development challenge? (name the goal, two words)
questions.explanation: The report identifies SDG 2, Zero Hunger, as India's most critical development challenge.

quizzes.title: Climate Finance: Sources and Funds
quizzes.passage:
Climate finance refers to money that supports action against climate change, and it can come from local, national or transnational sources. Such action has two broad aims: reducing emissions, and helping communities adapt to the effects of climate change. Several multilateral funds have been set up to channel resources to these aims, and each fund has its own role and procedures. Their approaches differ, and some are designed around the needs of particular groups of countries. The arrangements include a number of different funds, each with its own structure, which is why the subject can seem complex.

Climate finance also rests on a set of principles that guide how responsibility is shared among countries. These principles reflect the fact that countries do not all contribute to the problem in the same way. Climate finance is discussed as part of the global response to climate change, and it is closely linked with the commitments that countries make in their national climate plans.

The system is not without difficulties. The funding that countries need for their climate plans does not always match what is available to them. The arrangements are still developing, and new funds continue to be considered as the global response evolves.

questions.q: In which year did the Global Environment Facility become the operating entity of the financial mechanism?
questions.explanation: The Global Environment Facility became the operating entity of the financial mechanism in 1994.

questions.q: Which fund gives developing countries full ownership of adaptation projects?
questions.explanation: The Adaptation Fund gives developing countries full ownership of adaptation projects.

questions.q: Along with CBDR-RC, which principle forms part of the principles of climate finance?
questions.explanation: Polluter Pays is listed alongside Common but Differentiated Responsibility and Respective Capability as a principle of climate finance.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): Multilateral climate funds are coordinated by the UNFCCC.
Reason (R): The Green Climate Fund was established in 2010 at COP 16.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the founding year of the Green Climate Fund does not explain why the UNFCCC coordinates the funds.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Global Environment Facility   ->   C. Emission-reduction projects in developing nations
II. Clean Development Mechanism   ->   A. Financial assistance to nations most affected by climate change
III. Green Climate Fund   ->   B. Operating entity of the financial mechanism
IV. Loss and Damage Fund   ->   D. Houses the LDCF and SCCF funds
questions.explanation: The Global Environment Facility is the operating entity (B), the CDM funds emission cuts (C), the GCF houses the LDCF and SCCF (D), and the Loss and Damage Fund gives assistance (A).

questions.q:
Read the statements below:
I. Climate finance can be drawn from public, private or alternative sources.
II. The Adaptation Fund is coordinated by the Clean Development Mechanism.
III. Least Developed Countries receive much less approved funding per capita from multilateral climate funds.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and III match the booklet, while the Adaptation Fund is coordinated by the UNFCCC, not the Clean Development Mechanism.

questions.q:
Examine the following:
I. The Loss and Damage Fund was set up in 2023.
II. The Green Climate Fund was established in 2015.
III. A slow rate of approvals is listed as a challenge to climate finance.
Which option gives the number of correct statements?
questions.explanation: Only statements I and III are correct, since the Green Climate Fund was established in 2010, not 2015.

quizzes.title: Climate Finance Funds and Principles
quizzes.passage:
Climate finance covers money that is spent on action against climate change, whether the funding comes from local, national or transnational sources. Such action has two main aims, namely reducing the emissions that cause warming and adapting to the changes that warming brings. A number of multilateral funds have been created to channel resources to these aims, and they operate under different arrangements. Some funds are linked to specific groups of countries. The arrangements are complex, and each fund works through its own rules for deciding which projects to support.

Climate finance is also guided by a set of principles about how responsibility should be shared between countries. These principles reflect the idea that countries have different levels of capability and different histories of contribution to the problem.

In practice, the system has faced difficulties. The funding that countries need under their own climate plans does not always match the money available to them. Projects can take a long time to be approved, and some groups of countries receive less approved funding in relation to their population than others. New funds continue to be set up to respond to particular needs, so the arrangements are still developing.

questions.q: Which fund, set up in 2023, provides financial assistance to nations most affected by climate change? (name the fund)
questions.explanation: The Loss and Damage Fund, set up in 2023, provides financial assistance to nations most affected by climate change.

questions.q: In which year did the Global Environment Facility become the operating entity of the financial mechanism? (year)
questions.explanation: The Global Environment Facility became the operating entity of the financial mechanism in 1994.

questions.q: Which principle, along with CBDR-RC, is a principle of climate finance? (two words)
questions.explanation: Polluter Pays is one of the two principles of climate finance listed with CBDR-RC.

questions.q: Which fund, established at COP 16 in 2010, houses the LDCF and SCCF? (name the fund)
questions.explanation: The Green Climate Fund, established in 2010 at COP 16, houses the LDCF and SCCF.

questions.q: Which body coordinates multilateral climate funds? (acronym)
questions.explanation: Multilateral climate funds are coordinated by the UNFCCC.

questions.q: What is the mechanism that carries out emission-reduction projects in developing nations? (acronym)
questions.explanation: The Clean Development Mechanism, abbreviated CDM, carries out emission-reduction projects in developing nations.

questions.q: Which fund gives developing countries full ownership of adaptation projects? (name it, two words)
questions.explanation: The Adaptation Fund gives developing countries full ownership of adaptation projects.

quizzes.title: Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0
quizzes.passage:
Gram Panchayats and other traditional local bodies form the base of rural governance, and a nationwide framework now assesses how these bodies perform. Each local body is evaluated and placed in a grade that reflects its standing against the framework's benchmarks. The framework relies on indicators that can be checked, so that the results rest on evidence rather than impressions.

The framework is also aligned with the global development agenda. It takes the broad global goals and turns them into a smaller set of goals that suit village-level planning. Thematic areas are part of the assessment as well, and these cover subjects such as livelihoods and health in rural communities. Results so far show that Tripura has the largest share of local bodies in the upper grades.

The grades form an ordered scale. They run from the highest tier, which is reserved for the strongest performance, down to the lowest tier. Each tier gives local bodies a clear reference point. The approach is nationwide, and it applies to Gram Panchayats across the country, which means that the same framework is used for bodies in every part of the country.

questions.q: Which grade is awarded for a composite score of 60 to 74?
questions.explanation: A composite score of 60 to 74 earns the Performer (B) grade.

questions.q: Into how many localised SDGs does the index translate the 17 SDGs?
questions.explanation: The index translates the 17 SDGs into 9 localised Sustainable Development Goals.

questions.q: Which ministry localises the SDGs through the Panchayat Advancement Index?
options: Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj localises the SDGs through the index and its thematic indicator framework.

questions.q:
Assertion (A): The Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0 uses objective and verifiable indicators.
Reason (R): The index grades local bodies on a composite score from 0 to 100.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation: Both statements are true, but the 0 to 100 scoring range does not explain why the index uses verifiable indicators.

questions.q:
Match List I with List II:
I. Achiever (A+)   ->   B. Score of 60 to 74
II. Front Runner (A)   ->   A. Score below 40
III. Performer (B)   ->   D. Score of 75 to 89
IV. Beginner (D)   ->   C. Score above 90
questions.explanation: Achiever is above 90 (C), Front Runner is 75 to 89 (D), Performer is 60 to 74 (B), and Beginner is below 40 (A).

questions.q:
Read the statements below:
I. The index is recognised as the first comprehensive index globally to evaluate rural local governance.
II. No Gram Panchayat reached the Achiever category.
III. The index translates the 17 SDGs into 17 localised goals.
Which of the above statements is/are correct?
questions.explanation: Statements I and II match the booklet, while the 17 SDGs are translated into 9 localised SDGs, not 17.

questions.q:
Examine the following:
I. Grades are assigned on the basis of a composite score.
II. The Achiever grade applies to scores above 90.
III. The index is called Panchayat Advancement Index 3.0.
Which option gives the number of correct statements?
questions.explanation: Only statements I and II are correct, since the index is the Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0, not 3.0.

quizzes.title: Local Governance Grades and Goals
quizzes.passage:
Gram Panchayats and other traditional local bodies are the foundation of rural governance in India, and their performance is now assessed through a nationwide framework. The framework checks how well each body is doing in the areas that matter for local development, and it places each body in one of several grades. The assessment uses indicators that can be verified, which means that the results can be checked against evidence. Each local body receives a composite result based on these indicators, and that result determines its grade.

The grades run from the highest level to the lowest, which gives every body a clear benchmark. The framework is also tied to the Sustainable Development Goals, since it turns the global goals into a smaller set of goals suited to villages. Thematic areas form part of the assessment, covering themes such as livelihoods and healthy communities.

The framework is intended for Gram Panchayats and Traditional Local Bodies alike. Because it is nationwide, it applies across the country, and its grading scale gives local bodies in every state the same set of levels to aim for. Its purpose is to show where each body stands on the indicators it measures.

questions.q: What is the maximum composite score on which the index is based? (number)
questions.explanation: The composite score runs from 0 to 100.

questions.q: Into how many localised SDGs does the index translate the 17 SDGs? (number)
questions.explanation: The index translates the 17 SDGs into 9 localised Sustainable Development Goals.

questions.q: Which ministry localises the SDGs through this index? (name the ministry)
questions.explanation: The Ministry of Panchayati Raj localises the SDGs through the index.

questions.q: Above what score is the Achiever (A+) grade awarded? (number)
questions.explanation: The Achiever (A+) grade is awarded for scores above 90.

questions.q: Which grade is awarded to scores of 60 to 74? (grade name)
questions.explanation: Scores of 60 to 74 earn the Performer (B) grade.

questions.q: Which index is described as the first comprehensive index globally to evaluate rural local governance? (name it, with version)
questions.explanation: The Panchayat Advancement Index 2.0 is recognised as the first comprehensive index globally to evaluate rural local governance.

questions.q: Which grade is given for a composite score of 75 to 89? (grade name)
questions.explanation: A composite score of 75 to 89 earns the Front Runner (A) grade.
